explanation: Revise the grasp stage from the acknowledged frame-54 open hover, without restarting either tracker or weakening its failed 6 mm support criterion. Four individually described printed landmarks, selected and measured independently in two dimensions, replace the rejected automatic registration as the local correspondence method. Initial geometry is reused only at its unchanged physical frame; fresh depth and identity observations then validate each action boundary. The method first approaches a noncontact waypoint, reassesses the narrow finite-pad interval, and only closes if fresh visible passages and actual numerical contact margins pass. One close and one keep are followed, resources permitting, by two measured diagnostic lifts. Any slice exhaustion yields with actual phase, target and receipts; it does not imply grasp success. No later-stage control is included.
interface: Complete executable Python main(api) using the supplied API, np, math and geo. Returns stage_status, reason, JSON-compatible evidence, handoff and completion_proposed=false. Writes grasp_direct_v4 and preserves grasp_recovery_v3 and earlier checkpoints. The new checkpoint records inherited acknowledged execution; the rejected registration diagnosis; frame-54 shape and visible-side provenance; four persistent material-landmark labels and measured reference points; fresh point records and fits; clearance/overlap bounds; pending intent and actual receipt/state; closure delivery; and lift baselines/tests. A duplicate execution detects its checkpoint and does not replay physical actions. Unreceipted intents or unexplained entry motion block automatic continuation. At most 22 Jev calls and 66 native steps occur in this slice, below 24/72. Observation calls retain a two-review supervision reserve, permit at most two alternative measurement attempts overall, and inspect membership and measurement_errors before geometry. All measurements remain frame-labelled. Handoff contains data and assumptions, not future control code.
jev_protocol: All physical actions pass through api.control and real Jev. Exactly seven authored questions bind x/y/z to the corresponding world translation goal_relation, rx/ry/rz to the corresponding world rotation-vector goal_relation, and gripper to objective.gripper. Negative decreases the specified world component, positive increases it, and hold means within tolerance. Open, close and keep mean their requested deliveries; this method never requests open. Jev receives source-labelled measured geometry, the finite-pad candidate, the observation frame and the current phase. The host adds actual robot state and residuals. Jev selects directions and gripper commands unchanged; it is not a sensor, metric calculator, contact verifier or grasp detector. Individual controls use three native steps, translation limits of 20 mm for the free approach, 8 mm for low descent and 15 mm for diagnostic lifts, a 0.03 rad rotation limit, and phase-specific position tolerances of 3, 0.5 and 1.5 mm with 0.01 rad orientation tolerance. Every intent is checkpointed before dispatch and every returned receipt afterward. The first stall, opposed translation choice, gripper mismatch, failed actual finger/table margin or resource boundary stops further control. The 6 mm table clearance, 3 mm common vertical overlap, at least 1 mm surface allowance and 0.6 mm reserve at each end of the contact-height interval are preserved. Direct landmarks require at least 6 mm in-plane spread in both directions; table samples require 15 mm spread, and both plane RMS values must be at most 1.5 mm. Rejected tracker support is never reclassified as adequate. Fresh reviews identify surfaces and visible passages; numerical helpers calculate geometry. Neither reaching a pose nor delivering close establishes retention. stage_complete requires two separate fresh RGB-D correspondence tests with at most 5 mm attachment discrepancy, measured upward material/hand motion, visible table separation and no apparent slip. Occlusion or ambiguous landmarks permits only a bounded different-camera measurement, otherwise an explicit gap with the current gripper preserved. Slice exhaustion returns yield, and whole-task completion is always false.
